# beowulf-fitt-06 — review

Method: every note read against its own line; Old English to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; `i` for remembered English; published parts grepped (fitts I–V, glossary) for house renderings. `t` and `ln` untouched (verified by script against a copy of the draft).

### Considered and refused

- 391 'hēt' "bade" in `l` vs "bids me" in `i`: idiomatic for a herald; sense identical.
- 373 'tō hām forgeaf' as "gave in marriage": the note's claim stands; `i` adds "as his wife" which the idiom supports.
- 377 'Ðonne' "Moreover" in `i` vs "Then": note already calls the reading uncertain.
- 407 `i` drops "young" of 'magoðegn': note explains the choice.
- 408 "usual way for a warrior to name his credentials": unverifiable generalisation but harmless; kept.
- 445 "You will have no need to hide my head" and 438 "foe against foe": near any translation because the grammar leaves little choice; rebuilt in thought from the case endings, kept.
- 450 `l` "no, you need not": `nō … ne` doubled negation cannot be shown literally without gibberish.
- 401 `i` "to guard" for asyndetic 'hēoldon': purpose reading is idiomatic and the note describes the asyndeton.
- 454 'Hrǣdlan' = Hrēþel: note already says "probably".
- 407 'wæs' as imperative and 442 "Wēn’ ic" elision: both match the apparatus and glossary.
- No dot under a vowel occurs in this part, so no metrical-dot sentence is needed.

### Notable for later passes

- Cruces, all flagged in the notes: 'fīfe geband' (420, disputed reading; a QUESTIONS.md entry is called for by the conventions and is not yet there), 'heo[r]ðe' (404, vs Bugge's 'hlēoðe'), 'wonhȳdum' (434), 'mearcað mōrhopu' (450), 'mægenhrēð' (445), 'Gēotena' (443), 'ealdfæder' (373), 'sibbegedriht' (387), 'mōdþræce' (384), 'ārstafum' (382), 'unforhte' (444, adjective or adverb).
- Glosser (pass 2): 'unforhte' parse; 'þyrse' dative; 'feorme' accusative; 'āglǣcan' = the awesome one; 'mīn[n]e' masc. acc. agreeing with 'cræft'; 'heregrīman' dative plural; 'lāþum' sg or pl.

## Pass 2

Method: every note re-read against its line; Old English to `l` word by word; `l` against `i`; `i` for remembered English; published parts checked for cross-references (262, 316, 320, 333/334, 363 confirmed) and house renderings; then every novel parse in `gloss.json` checked against each line it occurs in, every known form checked for coverage (`known-forms.json` against the root glossary), and every `__broaden__` entry checked to carry the old entry whole plus ' · '. `t`, `ln` and `p` verified identical to the pre-pass file by script; `gloss.json` keys unchanged except six new `__broaden__` keys; JSON valid; no line numbers in entries.

### Checked and found correct (no change)

Every other parse in `gloss.json` was checked against its line(s): case, number, tense and mood of all remaining novel forms (e.g. ‘þyrse’ dative, ‘āglǣcan’ dative, ‘heregrīman’ dative plural, ‘mīn[n]e’ with ‘cræft’, ‘feorme’ accusative after ‘ymb’, ‘lāþum’ ambiguous). The nineteen original broadenings (fāh, geogoþe, grendel, healle, hēap, lāð, mīne, scyld, sōhte, wille, wið, wæs, wēan, wēn, ðǣm, þonne, þām, þē, þǣm) keep the old entry whole.

### Considered and refused

- 442 ‘unforhte’: kept as adverb in `l`/`i` (pass 1); the form in -e fits an adverb, and the note gives the adjective reading. Not re-opened.
- 419–420 ‘fīfe geband’: kept as "bound five"; the reading is Klaeber's, the apparatus alternatives (‘fīfel’, ‘fīfelgeban’, ‘fīfla gebann’) are in the note; no other reading is rendered because none is established.
- 372 ‘cnihtwesende’ agreeing with ‘hine’: the ending is not the usual accusative -ne, so it could be nominative; but the sense (he was the boy) fixes it. Kept.
- 419 `l` "themselves saw it": "it" is supplied for the objectless ‘ofersāwon’; the note says no object is stated. Kept.
- 391 `i` "bids me tell you": herald's present for ‘hēt’; refused in pass 1 and again.
- 435/437/438/445/450 phrases near other renderings ("foe against foe", "strength of thirty men in his hand-grip", "no need to hide my head", "to eat the Geat folk"): the case endings leave almost no alternative; refused as echoes.
- 415 `l` ‘þēoden’ "prince" vs fitt-05's "lord" in the vocative: `l` and `i` are both fine; not a house formula.
- 408 note's "usual way for a warrior to name his credentials": unverifiable but harmless; kept.
- ‘sōhte’ broadening carries a third sense (3rd sg preterite, 376) beside the root entry: redundant but not wrong; kept.
- ‘sēlesta’ -a ending: a weak -a with a neuter noun is irregular; not emended (apparatus silent).
- No dot under a vowel in this part; no metrical-dot sentence is needed. No Fitt XXIX/XXX duty.

### Cruces left flagged (also in QUESTIONS.md)

fīfe geband (419–420, disputed), heo[r]ðe (404 vs Bugge's hlēoðe), wonhȳdum (433/434), mearcað mōrhopu (450), mægenhrēð (445), unforhte (444), Gēotena (443), ealdfæder (373), sibbegedriht (387), mōdþræce (384), ārstafum (382), haðor (414).
